projects.name: Rubrik DR backup

notes.text: Status email rates project ON-TRACK. IOSP-1011 (Pure-based backup enabled and ran for several days, Earle) and IOSP-1014 (confirm Pure backup works, Calvin) reported completed.
Transcript confirms Pure backup ran OK for several days with no issues; Earle and Calvin agreed IOSP-1011 and IOSP-1014 can be considered passed.

Timeline per status email: IOSP-1012 enable Rubrik RAC backup 10/16 18:00 UTC (Sri); IOSP-880 run/validate RAC backup and replication 10/17-10/20; IOSP-1013 prepare appliances for shutdown and Manchester deployment 10/21 (Sri, Calvin); IOSP-1010 shipment plan and contracts from 10/21 TBD (Karl/Calvin, procurement); IOSP-1015 international shipment Oct 27-Nov 9 (logistics); IOSP-1009 background DBA work Oct 23-Nov 23 (Earle); IOSP-1004/1005 rack and cable Nov 9-16 (Manchester infra, Priya/Mena); IOSP-1006 commissioning Nov 16-Dec 6 (Calvin, Sri); IOSP-1007 production testing Nov 30-Dec 6 (Calvin, Sri); IOSP-1008 fully production in Europe Dec 7.

Plan to enable Rubrik on the RAC instance this Friday (10/16, 18:00 UTC). First run expected about 16 hours based on the standalone run. Calvin recommended not accelerating it on a weekday; Mike Massimino and Karl Witt have low tolerance for production risk, so kickoff was set for Friday night.
notes.source: standup chat 2026-10-13 (Igor's own standup summary in notes-to-self) and rubrik chat 2026-10-13

notes.text: Earle agreed Rubrik on RAC can start Friday 10/16. Oracle backup runs on scdpcarac1 at 06:00 UTC; Rubrik backup to run at 18:00 UTC daily. Open question from Igor whether to reuse RM-1553 and COR-11600.
Igor reported 4 successful Pure backups, wanting 2 to 3 more, before activating Rubrik on RAC.

Karl Witt: a company is being contracted to pack and ship the gear; it will provide anything that needs signing. Calvin said the contracts (via MicroAge, work done by Tech X) are what hold up the shipment date and he will not move the date up until procurement signs. Appliance prep is a couple of hours (assign each of about 12 nodes a new IP and shut down).

Earle: DBA background work may start earlier than November; standby now running in Manchester and catching up; should be well underway by end of next week (10/23). Gabriel Rovira had no update on the EDB project.

Network gap found: the RAC hosts (scdpcarac1/2) have no interface on the CA Backup VLAN (130) that Rubrik uses (VLANs 130 and 2988). Calvin and Prajeet agree backup should use its own VLAN. Adding a VLAN interface on production scdpcarac1 requires an RM ticket and a maintenance window (maintenance Sunday 7PM Eastern, SREs incl. Ramana Chowdary). Rubrik would then start the initial run on Sunday instead of Friday; Earle suggested 13:00 UTC Sunday 10/18. Prajeet and Earle agreed to let the initial Rubrik run overlap the normal RMAN backup.

Open design question: how Rubrik connects to RAC (SCAN/VIP/host names) given Rubrik only talks on the backup VLANs and Oracle Clusterware will not manage a second VIP. Plan is to ask Rubrik Support and Oracle Support. Calvin will not create tickets until replies arrive.

Calvin posted network options (VLAN 130 Rubrik MCR cluster; options ranked most to least preferred) and later said Option 2 is supported by Rubrik (slightly different than stated, functionally equivalent).

Earle noted a needed step in the plan: successfully recover a Rubrik SASP backup onto bdddcanlora[3 or 5]. Igor asked when the SASP backup should happen as it had not been discussed in weekly calls; Earle said he had said 'Recover', discussed in nearly every meeting.

Igor and Aylin reviewed the old Confluence Rubrik page on goals and objectives; Igor added project objectives to epic IOSP-471 after double-checking with Calvin; asked about onboarding Postgres backups to Rubrik.

Prajeet shared RAC interface and VIP listing (scdpcarac1/2, VIPs) and said backup IPs do not need to be registered with Oracle Clusterware; Rubrik can be configured to recognize the RAC cluster and make both nodes eligible, per Rubrik docs.

Calvin: the standalone Oracle in Secaucus is only alive to support the Rubrik POC, so it can be decommissioned no later than the first week of November, possibly the last week of October. Not officially part of the Rubrik project.

Calvin's change for the maintenance window: based on Device42 and a ping test the IPs are not in use, but if the change is not completed during the maintenance window it pushes back Rubrik timelines. Martijn Katerbarg approved the change (RM number not stated in the message).
